Breaking: The mysterious golden shipwreck that led to decades of lawsuits

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1131 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Long before the Titanic, the most famous shipwreck in the US was the SS Central America.
  • Industry observers note that 425 people died.
  • Industry observers note that that loss of life alone should be reason enough for people to remember the ship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Long before the Titanic, the most famous shipwreck in the US was the SS Central America. The wooden steamship helped connect San Francisco with New York City before the construction of a coast-to-coast rail network, and sank off the coast of South Carolina in 1857.

Industry observers note that 425 people died. Most people today haven’t heard of it.

Industry observers note that that loss of life alone should be reason enough for people to remember the ship. But the SS Central America was also hauling $1.2 million worth of gold, according to a 1992 court case about the wreck. Given the current value of gold, that’s around $236 million in today’s dollars. And that’s just what’s documented: the ship had a number of wealthy passengers, who were likely carrying their own gold, so the total could be even higher.

A ship full of gold, sunk and lost for over a century. It’s odd that the ship isn’t a household name. And the story keeps getting weirder: the wreck contributed to a massive recession, and when treasure hunters found the ship in the 1980s, decades of lawsuits followed.

Say you wanted to get from San Francisco to New York City in the 1850s. Going over land was miserable—cars were a half century away, and there weren’t many roads. There wasn’t even a rail line connecting the two coasts. Your best bet was to take a ship down to what is now Panama, a train across that narrow bit of land, and then another ship up to New York.

It has been revealed that the SS Central America served the Atlantic part of that journey. It left the east coast of Panama on September 3, 1857, with 592 people on board. The ship had one other stop: Havana, Cuba. By September 8, when the ship was leaving that port, the weather looked great, according to a writeup by the US Naval Institute.

That changed—hurricane-force winds battered the wooden hull. By September 11, the crew was working to bail out the ship, and by noon every man joined them. It wasn’t enough: by 2pm the water reached the boilers, leaving the ship drifting. The bailing continued all night, and for a while it seemed like the weather would clear up long enough for a full evacuation. It wasn’t to be—the storm resumed by mid-morning. The captain signaled a nearby ship, the Marine, for help. Only 100 people—including the 59 women and children—boarded the Marine.

According to recent reports, the captain went down with the ship around 8pm local time, along with most of the remaining men, who were pulled in by the undertow of the sinking ship. The few men who survived did so by grabbing doors, chairs, and anything else still floating, until another ship—the Ellen—could find them. In total, 425 people lost their lives.

The human cost was high, but there was also a huge economic fallout. A 1992 paper by Lawrence D. Stone, the researcher whose work led to the rediscovery of the wreck, states that the gold on board was intended to shore up several banks already on the brink of collapse. Within a month, almost all banks in the US stopped offering gold in exchange for paper money.

Recent findings suggest that naturally, a ship this famous—with this much gold on board—became a bit of a legend. Countless people attempted to find the wreck, but no one succeeded until the Columbus-America Discovery Group of Ohio found the wreck in the 1980s. The crew was led by treasure hunter Tommy Gregory Thompson.

The discovery happened thanks to advanced technology—sonar and state-of-the-art remote-controlled submarines. But also because of math.

Stone, whose work I mentioned earlier, explained his method in a 1992 paper. He employed Bayesian search theory. This method begins with finding hypotheses about where the wreck may be, judging how likely each theory is, and ultimately making a map outlining the probability of the ship being in various areas. A route for the search is designed to start with the highest probability areas, continuing from there to lower probabilities.

The survey took 40 days, covering 1,400 square miles of ocean off the Carolina coast. The wreck ended up being in a relatively low probability area, though one included in the route. In 1988, a remotely operated vehicle provided a view of the wreck.

“The storybook result would have been for the Central America to have been found in a high probability area near the beginning of the search,” wrote Stone. “Given the actual result, what can we say about the value of the procedures for developing the search plan? The most obvious thing to say is that they worked.”.

In a recent development, that’s the thing about probability: the most likely thing isn’t always what’s true. That doesn’t mean it’s not worth calculating—it can still lead to good results.

In a recent development, but what about the gold? Over the next few years the team brought up most of the commercial gold shipment. A federal judge put its bullion value at about $21 million in 1993, but coins and ingots from a famous shipwreck are worth far more to collectors. In 2000, the bulk of it sold for about $50 million. Today most of the gold is in the hands of private collectors.

It has been revealed that this would normally be where the story ends: the treasure is found, the treasure hunters get paid, and everyone is happy. That’s not what happened this time.

Recent findings suggest that by 1989, the insurance companies that covered the SS Central America back in the 1850s argued that the gold belonged to them. Their logic: We paid damages to clients who lost the gold, therefore it’s ours. The insurance companies lost that lawsuit, but it was only the beginning.

Sources indicate that thompson took $12.5 million from investors to fund the treasure hunt. Those investors sued in 2005, alleging they never got any proceeds from the treasure, even after the 2000 sale of the gold. Several members of Thompson’s crew sued in 2006. Thompson went into hiding in 2012, only to be arrested in 2015. He wasn’t released until March of 2026. Some 500 gold coins remain unaccounted for.

Recent findings suggest that it’s an odd footnote to a fascinating story of history, math, and science. And who knows? Maybe this story will still be going a hundred years in the future.

Industry observers note that and there may be more to the story of the SS Central America. A 2018 expedition recovered more gold from a safe on the ship, in a passenger compartment. There could be more down there.

Finding the right fitness tracker is less about buying the most advanced wearable out there and more about choosing the one that will actually work for how you’ll use it to help you meet your fitness goals. You may want a smartwatch that can handle calls and texts along with fitness data tracking, or maybe you’re looking for a distraction-free screenless band that quietly tracks your metrics in the background. If running is your thing, you may want a smartwatch with GPS accuracy and real-time training metrics that are easy to read during a run, and if you’re focused on improving sleep, you may prefer a smart ring that won’t feel bulky overnight.

For this guide, we considered a range of fitness trackers for different training styles and tracking needs, from simple bands for everyday activity tracking to running watches, smartwatches, screenless wearables, and smart rings, all designed to monitor sleep, recovery, fitness, and health trends over time.

Whoop earned the top spot for the best overall fitness tracker because it provides deeper understanding of your data while also giving context of what all that data means. I’ve been using a Whoop for the past several years, and of all the fitness tracker options I’ve tested, it remains my hands-down favorite. It delivers some of the most useful recovery, sleep, and strain insights in a distraction-free design that’s so comfortable I often completely forget that I’m wearing it. The battery life is impressive, and I only have to charge mine twice a month.

Whoop 5.0 is built on the foundation of an app that offers analysis of your metrics paired with context, so you actually learn what all the numbers mean for your health and training. The screen-free design means that instead of buzzing constantly or encouraging you to check another display, it quietly tracks your metrics in the background and turns that data into recovery, strain, sleep data to give you an overall picture of your fitness within an app.

The sensor platform uses multi-wavelength optical heart rate sensors, skin-temperature sensing, blood oxygen monitoring, and accelerometer and gyroscope motion sensors to collect data continuously, tracking your resting heart rate, heart rate variability, respiratory rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature, sleep stages, strain, and recovery.

The app then interprets those numbers, in a way that feels more actionable than raw data alone, to generate a daily readiness score that indicates how much physical exertion your body is up for on any given day (00033though it’s always important to listen to your body regardless of what a wearable claims). If you wake up with a low recovery score, for example, Whoop may recommend reducing workout intensity. If your sleep debt is climbing, it will show how much rest you need to get back on track.

It also offers other behavior change suggestions that could improve how you feel based on the data it collects about you and your habits over time. In fact, the in-depth habit tracking feature offers some of the most valuable insights into how day-to-day behaviors affect us physiologically. As a trainer, this has been one of the features I've seen make the most long-term impact with clients, as it really helps them connect the dots and understand how everything is interrelated.

Sources indicate that whoop 5.0 does require a membership and there are three different tiers, the main difference being the level of insights and analysis. Whoop One covers the core Whoop experience, including sleep, strain, recovery, steps, activity monitoring, heart-rate tracking, and women’s hormonal insights, which helps us see how menstrual cycle phases may relate to sleep, recovery, and performance. Whoop Peak adds a broader health and wellness layer, including health monitor, stress monitor, healthspan, and more advanced coaching-style insights for users who want to connect daily habits with longer-term performance and recovery trends (this is the tier I personally go with). Whoop Life is the most advanced tier, adding heart-health features such as ECG, irregular heart rhythm notifications, and blood pressure insights where available. Ultimately, the difference between the tiers is less about the tracker experience itself and more about how much interpretation, health context, and advanced monitoring you want.

The tradeoff is cost. Since Whoop uses a membership model, it will end up being more expensive over time than a tracker that doesn’t require a subscription. It also is not the best choice if you want live pace, distance, or workout stats on your wrist during a run. For that, a Garmin, Apple Watch, Samsung Galaxy Watch, or COROS watch will be more practical.

Recent findings suggest that the Google Fitbit Inspire earned its spot as the best budget pick because it gives you the core fitness-tracking features most people want in a slim and approachable design. It’s not trying to be a full smartwatch or a performance running watch. Instead, it focuses on the basics: steps, heart rate, workouts, sleep, active minutes, and general wellness trends.

That simplicity makes the Fitbit Inspire a good entry point for someone who wants to become more aware of their fitness data without getting buried in advanced metrics. It can track walks, gym workouts, casual runs, and sleep, while the Fitbit app makes the data easy to understand. You can quickly see how much movement you got throughout the day, how long you slept, and how your habits are trending over time. Additionally, you’ll get a stress management score, guided breathing sessions, and reminders to move.

It is also one of the easiest trackers to wear all day. The band is slim enough to feel less bulky than a smartwatch, and the display is small but still easy to use for checking basic stats. If your main goals are walking more, staying accountable, improving sleep habits, or getting started with activity tracking, the Inspire offers strong value.

In a recent development, the main limitation is that it’s not necessarily built for serious training. Depending on the model, the GPS may rely on your phone rather than being fully built into the device, and runners who want advanced pace analysis, training load, recovery guidance, or race tools will likely outgrow it. But for the price, it’s one of the most practical fitness trackers for everyday use.

It has been revealed that the Apple Watch Series 12 blends health tracking, workout features, smartwatch convenience, and safety tools better than almost any other wearable. If you already use an iPhone, this is the most seamless option in our guide.

The Series 12 features more advanced sensor capabilities, including an upgraded optical heart sensor that measures heart rate every five seconds, and tracks HRV more frequently. WH associate fitness editor Addison Aloin wrote in her review that the Series 12 has “a great baseline of health and fitness features.”.

In a recent development, the Series 12 tracks a wide range of workouts, including running, walking, cycling, strength training, HIIT, yoga, Pilates, swimming, hiking, and many more. During activity, the display is bright and you can easily view data like pace, distance, heart rate, time, and workout zones during runs and workouts. It also integrates smoothly with Apple Fitness+, the Health app, and third-party training apps.

It has been revealed that one of the most meaningful updates the Series 12 got is a upcoming readiness score, which uses recent activity, training load, your sleep score, and overnight metrics like heart rate, respiratory rate, skin temperature, and recovery HRV to estimate how prepared your body is for exertion. The score runs from 0 to 10 and gives you a recommendation for your day, such as Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready, or Go For It. “My only complaint is that it’s kind of hard to find the readiness score on the watch and in the Health app,” Aloin indicates.

Since it’s so much more than just a tracker you wear during workout, the Apple Watch also offers a lot of versatility. It can handle notifications, calls, music, maps, timers, contactless payments, fall detection, and emergency features, making it a strong option for anyone who wants one device that can move between workouts and everyday life.

Recent findings suggest that it is also a good pick for people who like motivational nudges. Apple’s activity rings are simple, visual, and surprisingly effective if you respond well to daily goals. If you want coaching-style feedback without digging through complex training dashboards, the Series 12’s newer software can translate health and fitness data into easily digestible prompts.

It has been revealed that the Series 12 offers up to 24 hours of everyday battery life, and Apple says 15 minutes of charging can add up to 12 hours of battery. That makes it more manageable for overnight sleep tracking, but it still requires more planning than fitness trackers that last several days or longer on a single charge. “I’ve found the battery life is awesome for everyday use, but usually does need a charge every other day or so,” Aloin says.

Sources indicate that read More: Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Ultra 4.

According to recent reports, the Google Fitbit Air gives you the quiet, distraction-free experience of a screenless wearable at a more approachable price point than premium recovery bands. The Fitbit Air tracks core metrics like activity, heart rate, sleep, and wellness trends over time, then sends that information to your phone.

Since there’s no screen, you’re not checking your wrist throughout the day. That makes it a strong option for anyone who wants to be more mindful about movement and sleep but doesn’t want a smartwatch. It’s also a good fit for people who are curious about screenless tracking but are not ready to commit to a more expensive platform. It offers a simpler, lower-pressure way to see whether passive health tracking actually helps your routine.

Industry observers note that the Fitbit app is another advantage. Fitbit’s platform is approachable, especially for beginners, and tends to present health data in a way that feels less intimidating than more athlete-focused apps. That makes the Air a strong choice for casual users who want guidance without performance overload.

Industry observers note that the main limitation is that a screenless budget tracker will not replace a running watch or smartwatch. You will not get the same real-time workout stats, app support, phone features, or advanced training analysis. But if you want affordable, low-distraction tracking, Fitbit Air is a compelling pick.

Recent findings suggest that the Coros Pace 4 is our best lightweight pick because it delivers serious training features in a watch that feels easy to wear. After testing the watch for two months, MH deputy features editor Carina Hsieh stated that it feels so lightweight that you forget it’s there. It’s especially appealing for runners and fitness-minded owners who want more data than a basic tracker can provide but don’t want a bulky smartwatch.

Coros has built a strong reputation among runners because its watches tend to offer excellent battery life, practical training tools, and reliable GPS. The Pace 4 continues that tradition. “I was pleasantly surprised by how responsive and quick the GPS signal was on runs,” Hsieh stated. She also noted that the watch had an exceptionally long battery life during her testing, and that she only had to charge it twice in two months.

For runners, the Pace 4 can track pace, distance, heart rate, route data, workouts, recovery, and training trends. Features like race predictions, virtual pacing, breadcrumb navigation, and personalized training tools make it feel like a strong contender for anyone who is a serious runner. It is also useful for people who cross-train, since it can handle gym workouts, cycling, walking, and other activities.

Recent findings suggest that A big reason to choose the Pace 4 over other smartwatches is that it feels purpose-built for fitness. You’re not paying for a huge app ecosystem or phone-like features. Instead, you’re getting a lightweight training watch that can help you understand your fitness, recovery, and progress.

According to recent reports, the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 is the best fitness tracker for Android owners, especially anyone with a Samsung Galaxy phone. It offers a polished smartwatch experience with robust health and fitness tools, making it a bit like an Android equivalent to the Apple Watch. WH beauty editor Nicole Saunders, who has tested multiple wearables over the years, states she usually struggles to wear trackers consistently because the bands were uncomfortable overnight. But the Galaxy Watch 9 changed that. “The band is surprisingly comfortable to wear and, dare I say, actually looks good,” she mentioned.

Industry observers note that this smartwatch tracks everyday activity, steps, heart rate, workouts, stress, sleep, and recovery-style metrics. It also includes Samsung’s Vitals feature, which monitors overnight patterns including heart rate, respiratory rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature, and other sleep-related signals, then compares them against your personal baseline. Saunders says it took about a full week for her baseline to set up, and anything outside of her normal range appeared in orange in the app, making it easy to compare metrics and spot subtle changes over time.

In a recent development, it also tracks a wide range of exercise modes, and its running features are useful for people who want coaching-style tools. Samsung’s body composition measurement feature can also be helpful for observing trends over time, though the numbers should be treated as estimates rather than medical-grade measurements. Saunders also liked the sleep features, including sleep quality tracking and snore detection, which she found both funny and potentially useful for better understanding nighttime habits.

The watch pairs easily with Galaxy phones, and the Samsung Health app organizes fitness and wellness data in an approachable way. If you want a tracker that can monitor workouts in the morning, handle notifications during the day, and track sleep at night, the Galaxy Watch 9 is a strong choice. In her testing, Saunders found it to be stylish and effective, adding that it would make a great gift for someone starting a health journey or looking for more detailed insights.

The Oura Ring 5 offers robust health and sleep tracking in the most discreet package of all the fitness trackers in this guide. If you don’t like wearing a watch around the clock or simply prefer jewelry over a wristband, Oura is the easiest fitness tracker to live with. In her review, WH associate editor Olivia Luppino said it’s the only fitness tracker she’s ever used that she hasn’t wanted to take off.

The Oura Ring’s biggest strength is passive health tracking. It’s designed to unobtrusively monitor your body in the background, and then translate that information into readiness, sleep, activity, stress, temperature, and recovery insights in an easy to use app. It can be especially helpful for people who want to understand how sleep, illness, stress, menstrual cycle changes, and daily habits affect energy.

For sleep tracking, the Ring 5 is one of the more comfortable options since a ring is less bulky than a watch, and many people find it easier to wear overnight. The app also makes sleep data easy to understand, showing not just how long you slept but how restorative that sleep may have been.

Industry observers note that the tradeoff is workout tracking. Oura can track activity and has improved its fitness features, but it’s still not the best choice for people who want real-time stats during runs, strength workouts, or cycling sessions. It can also interfere with grip during weightlifting and kettlebell training. If you want to glance at pace, heart rate, or intervals mid-workout, choose a watch. If you want discreet, all-day and all-night health tracking, choose a smart ring.

For runners, the Garmin Forerunner 570 sits in a sweet spot between advanced training watches and an everyday wearable. Garmin makes several excellent Forerunner models, but the 570 offers a mix of running metrics, GPS tools, recovery insights, smartwatch features, and comfortable wearability for runners who want more than the basics without jumping straight to flagship option.

The Forerunner 570 is designed to be useful for structured training with its capability to track runs, intervals, long runs, tempo sessions, races, recovery runs, and cross-training workouts. It also gives runners access to Garmin’s broader training ecosystem, including performance metrics, suggested workouts, recovery guidance, HRV status, sleep data, training readiness-style insights, and race-related tools. For someone training for a 5K, half marathon, marathon, or simply trying to become a more consistent runner, those features can be super useful.

In a recent development, it has a bright AMOLED display, touchscreen support as well as physical buttons, a feature that’s especially notable for runners since touchscreens can sometimes be frustrating with sweat, rain, or gloves. Battery life varies from 8 hours to up to 10 days depending on how many features you’re using.

Industry observers note that the biggest drawback is price. Though it’s not the priciest Forerunner offering out there, the Forerunner 570 is not inexpensive, and newer runners who only want pace, distance, and heart rate may be perfectly happy with a more affordable Forerunner model. But runners who want a capable watch they won’t outgrow, the 570 is a great option.

According to recent reports, the Garmin Cirqa is the best screenless tracker for lovers of the Garmin fitness ecosystem, since it integrates seamlessly with Garmin’s other tech. It delivers health and activity tracking without adding another display to your life, and is especially well suited for anyone who wants to use Garmin Connect but doesn't want to wear a full Garmin watch all day long.

Sources indicate that that makes Cirqa especially useful for athletes who already own a Garmin running, cycling, or outdoor watch. You may want to wear your Forerunner for workouts and during runs, but prefer something smaller and screen-free for sleep, recovery, or everyday tracking. The Cirqa fills that gap.

Recent findings suggest that it also has a cost advantage over some screenless competitors because it doesn’t require a subscription. That makes it appealing for Garmin loyalists who want ongoing tracking without committing to a monthly membership.

The Cirqa isn’t the best choice if you want live workout stats, on-wrist coaching, or a display for pace and distance, and a Garmin watch would be better for that. But as a low-distraction daily tracker that complements Garmin’s training platform, Cirqa is a welcome addition to the category.

The Google Fitbit Edge bridges the gap between a simple Fitbit band and a full smartwatch, making it a strong choice if you want a display but don’t want a bulkier smartwatch. It gives you a screen for checking stats, starting workouts, reviewing progress, and seeing basic information at a glance.

Sources indicate that compared with the Fitbit Air, the Edge is more interactive, compared with the Inspire, it’s a more advanced option, and compared with a Pixel Watch, it’s simpler to use and more fitness focused. It offers enough features to be useful throughout the day, tracking activity, workouts, sleep, heart-rate trends, and daily wellness data, while still keeping the overall experience lighter than a smartwatch. If you want a compact Google Fitbit tracker with a screen and stronger features than the entry-level models, the Edge is the best fit.

Recent findings suggest that A good heart rate monitor is one of the most important features to look for in a fitness tracker, whether you’re training seriously or just getting started. Heart rate data can help you better understand exercise intensity, track effort during workouts, and monitor resting heart rate over time, which can be a useful marker of cardiovascular fitness. While wrist-based trackers typically aren’t as precise as chest straps, they can still offer a helpful read on exertion levels during moderate to intense activity, according to a 2019 study in Cardiovascular Diagnosis & Therapy.

Industry observers note that sleep tracking can be a useful feature because sleep plays a major role in recovery, energy, mood, and overall performance. By tracking patterns like sleep duration, consistency, and overnight restlessness, a fitness tracker can help you spot habits that may be affecting how you feel the next day. Many models also break down sleep stages, show trends over time, and offer recovery or readiness insights based on your nightly data. While the numbers aren’t always perfect, they can provide a helpful starting point for understanding your routine and making small changes, like adjusting bedtime, limiting late caffeine, or improving sleep consistency.

Weight may not seem that important at first, but it matters when you’re wearing a fitness tracker all day and night. A larger, heavier model can feel more noticeable over time, especially during sleep or long workouts. There’s no single ideal size, and the best option will depend on how you strategy to use it.

According to recent reports, if you run, hike, or spend a lot of time outdoors, it may be worth choosing a more durable model, even if it’s slightly bulkier. For everyday wear, walking, strength training, or mostly indoor workouts, a lighter, lower-profile tracker may be more comfortable. Ultimately, the right fit comes down to your activity level, wrist size, and what you’ll actually want to keep wearing.

Many of the best fitness trackers can run for days or even weeks on a single charge, such as the Whoop 5.0. But battery doesn't always equate to quality, given that an option like the Apple Watch Series 12 needs to be charged every day and it’s still one of our absolute favorites. Ultimately it comes down to how a trackers charging needs will fit into your routine.

In a recent development, as with all tech, you want a fitness tracker that’s easy to use. If your new tracker isn’t intuitive for you to set up or use daily, you’re far less likely to use it consistently. Ultimately, the only way to know for sure is to try it out yourself to see if it works for you. That's why it’s smart to buy a fitness tracker with a generous return policy.

In a recent development, I’ve been a certified personal trainer for more than a decade, and together with other Women’s Health editors, I’m constantly testing the latest fitness trackers across key factors like durability, comfort, features, and accuracy. We tested them during our workouts, on our runs, in Pilates class, and more. And of course, we tested them during sleep. Whether you’re training regularly or just want something for everyday activity tracking, the models we tested for the latest update range from basic fitness trackers to powerful smartwatches and everything in between.

Healthgrades Confirms Top Hospitals for Specialty Care, Outpatient Procedures

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that hospital ratings have become an key resource for choosing where to receive care.
  • On October 27, Healthgrades revealed the recipients of the 2027 Specialty Excellence Outpatient Awards and Specialty State Rankings.
  • According to recent reports, the annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hospital ratings have become an key resource for choosing where to receive care. They influence which doctors patients choose, how far they are willing to travel, and whether they seek care at a different facility.

On October 27, Healthgrades revealed the recipients of the 2027 Specialty Excellence Outpatient Awards and Specialty State Rankings.

According to recent reports, the annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States. Healthgrades is the leading platform used by Americans for finding a doctor or hospital.

New research from Healthgrades highlights that hospital quality is increasingly a factor in healthcare decisions.

Industry observers note that around 80% of patients report that when looking for a doctor, the quality of the hospital where they practice matters. Additionally, 7 in 10 patients (68%) say they’re more likely to seek care for a procedure or health condition from a doctor who works at a hospital with high quality ratings.

What’s more, around 71% of patients say they would switch doctors to gain access to a higher-rated hospital.

“Our specialty awards identify the nation’s top-performing hospitals across numerous medical specialties, helping consumers find high quality care tailored to their specific needs,” said Alana Biggers, MD, MPH, medical advisor at Healthgrades.

Recent findings suggest that healthgrades is owned by RVO Health. By clicking on this link, we may receive a commission. Learn more.

“Navigating the complex healthcare system can feel daunting, but taking a proactive stance to understand where to access superior care can enhance your healthcare journey and overall experience. The ability to make informed decisions about your health — and where to get care — is a cornerstone of self-advocacy, and we are proud to help make that information accessible to all patients.”.

Healthgrades identifies hospitals that deliver exceptional outcomes across common outpatient procedures and specialty conditions.

Finding high quality care is crucial, particularly amid a growing gap between top-performing and one-star hospitals.

According to Healthgrades, from 2023 to 2025, if all hospitals had performed at the five-star level from 2023 to 2025:.

“One of the biggest challenges is balancing increasing patient needs with the resources available to healthcare professionals,” Biggers noted.

“Hospitals face workforce shortages, growing administrative responsibilities, financial pressures, and increasing complexity in patient care. Physicians and other healthcare professionals need adequate time and support not only to evaluate and treat patients, but also to communicate results, coordinate follow-up care, and address concerns that arise between visits,” she continued.

“When healthcare teams are adequately supported, they are better positioned to communicate effectively with patients, coordinate care, and address patients’ needs.”.

Biggers remarked that ensuring equal access to quality healthcare is challenging because of factors such as:.

Hospital closures and reduced services make access even more difficult. Biggers identified a few possible solutions, such as expanding outpatient care, building community partnerships, using telehealth when appropriate, and improving coordination among healthcare providers.

“Ultimately, providing high quality care requires more than clinical expertise. It requires healthcare systems to invest in their workforce, strengthen care coordination, and create environments where healthcare professionals have the resources they need to provide safe, effective, and patient-centered care,” Biggers stated.

“Equally key, healthcare systems must ensure that patients have meaningful access to these services, regardless of where they live or their socioeconomic circumstances.”.

Healthgrades acknowledges hospitals that excel in three aspects of specialty care:.

Biggers said that outstanding hospitals recognize that high quality care extends beyond just treating an illness.

“It involves listening to patients, understanding their individual circumstances, and ensuring they feel respected, informed, and involved in their healthcare decisions,” she remarked.

Patients want to find a hospital that excels in the procedures or health conditions relevant to them.

The recipients of the Specialty Excellence Awards are among the top 15% of hospitals specializing in these areas.

Healthgrades evaluated patient outcomes at roughly 4,500 hospitals across 31 common procedures and conditions to reach their decisions.

Among the list of Specialty Excellence Award recipients, Healthgrades also recognizes America’s 100 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for 11 specialty areas andAmerica’s 50 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for four specialty areas.

“An outstanding hospital prioritizes both patient care and the people delivering that care,” Biggers told Healthline.

It has been revealed that “While clinical outcomes, patient safety, and access to evidence-based treatments are essential measures of quality, I believe hospitals must also invest in workforce development and support. This means ensuring physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals have appropriate staffing levels, adequate clinical and administrative support, and opportunities for continued professional development,” she continued.

Healthgrades awards U.S. hospitals that excel at Outpatient Orthopedic Surgery, Outpatient Joint Replacement, andOutpatient Prostate Care.

Industry observers note that outpatient care is one of the fastest-growing areas of healthcare. The number of orthopedic procedures performed in an outpatient environment has grown exponentially in recent years.

From 2020 to 2025, outpatient hip replacement procedures grew by 81%, while inpatient procedures dropped by 75%. Outpatient knee replacements increased by 71% while inpatient volumes decreased by 70%.

“I believe several factors are contributing to the growing demand for outpatient care, including advances in medical technology, a greater emphasis on preventive care, and the increasing need to manage chronic medical conditions,” Biggers said.

Industry observers note that “Many services and procedures that previously required hospitalization can now be safely performed in outpatient settings. Patients also appreciate the convenience of receiving care closer to home and avoiding unnecessary hospital stays,” she added.

To meet the increasing demand for outpatient procedures, Biggers cautioned that healthcare systems must ensure that these services are adequately staffed and supported.

“Effective communication and coordination between outpatient providers, specialists, and hospitals are essential to maintaining continuity and quality of care,” she remarked.

State Rankings identify the top three or five hospitals in eligible states across 19 key specialty areas.

Healthgrades is owned by RVO Health. By clicking on this link, we may receive a commission. Learn more.

The rankings are based on clinical performance and build on the 2027 Healthgrades Specialty Excellence Awards Methodology.

State-level specialty care rankings help consumers find outstanding local hospitals for their condition or procedure.

The analysis used Medicare inpatient data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) from 2023 to 2025, and assessed patient outcomes across 31 conditions and procedures.

These outcomes served as the foundation for determining Specialty Excellence Awards and state hospital rankings.

With consumer-facing awards and ratings influencing healthcare decisions, transparency about their methods and limitations remains essential.

Ratings can help patients ask better questions and compare options, but they should complement — not replace — clinical guidance and informed decision making.

The methodologies for each of the specialty awards can be found on the following pages:.

It has been revealed that for more information, Healthgrades’ Specialty Excellence Patient Advocate Center provides access to the information you need to make informed decisions about your care. This resource includes an overview of how Healthgrades picks award recipients, plus a list of the top U.S. hospitals for specialty care.

To be eligible for a Specialty Excellence Award, hospitals must receive a rating in the required procedures and conditions used to determine the award. Some awards are based on a single procedure, while others are based on a grouping of procedures. Breaking: BMW’s first US-built EV promises 456 miles of range and ultra-fast charging

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (767 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.
  • BMW officially opened its fresh Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.
  • The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-upcoming iX5 SUV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.

BMW officially opened its fresh Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.

The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-upcoming iX5 SUV.

The iX5 is being built about 15 miles away at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg, the company’s first fully electric model to be assembled in the US.

BMW Plant Spartanburg is churning out around 70 iX5s a day following a $1.7 billion investment in South Carolina to expand the plant for EV production and build the new battery assembly plant in Woodruff.

According to Robert Engelhorn, president and CEO of BMW Manufacturing in Spartanburg, the organization is confident the iX5 will attract buyers, promising 435 miles of range, ultra-fast charging, and its updated Neue Klasse technology and design.

Engelhorn told Automotive News in an interview that “there’s a clear trend globally for EVs,” adding that “We will contribute to this growth from the BMW side.”.

BMW didn’t provide a specific production estimate for the iX5, but suppliers were reportedly told it would be around 60,000 EVs in 2027, down from 100,000 it initially forecasted.

“We mentioned we would begin assembling fully electric BMW vehicles in the US by the end of 2026 – and we are delivering on that commitment,” Engelhorn said.

A organization spokesperson confirmed that the iX5 will initially use battery cells from China before switching to US-sourced cells from LG Energy Solutions plant in Arizona by the end of the decade.

With production now underway, the iX5 is expected to begin arriving at US dealerships in early 2027.

It has been revealed that the 2027 BMW iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800. BMW estimates the 144 kWh battery will provide up to 456 miles of range, up from the 435 miles it previously estimated.

Industry observers note that it features BMW’s upcoming “double-X” light signature, which combines the headlights, daytime running lights, side lights, and turn signals into one unit. The Double-X headlights come standard, but BMW remarked you can switch them for simpler diagonal stripes.

Last month, BMW showcased the i5’s ultra-fast-charging capabilities during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic.

During the demo, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW said enables it to add an impressive up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.

According to recent reports, the electric SUV features a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain setup that delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW says it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

According to recent reports, inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design and tech, like the smaller iX3 SUV. The setup includes a upcoming 17.9″ infotainment touchscreen and BMW’s Panoramic Vision, which spans the bottom of the windshield. There’s also an optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

This is at the top of our short list. Out of Spec got 411 miles at 70 mph (by contrast the Gravity rated at 450 got 368 on the same run and the R1S rated at 410 got 349). It is a real 400+ mile vehicle with an ability to charge a real 300 miles in ~20 minutes.

Edit: OOS was with 22" wheels rated at 426. It should get >430 with the standard 21" wheels.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, BMW’s upcoming iX5 is about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.

Industry observers note that by 2030, BMW plans to be assembling at least fully electric models at Plant Spartanburg. “This marks the beginning of the next chapter in the success story of the largest plant in our global production network,” Raymond Wittman, BMW’s head of production, noted.

Following Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany), and Shenyang (China), Woodruff is the fourth site in BMW’s production network to begin series production of the Gen6 batteries.

It has been revealed that travel is the daily gift of life, but that doesn’t mean travel can’t suck the life out of you, even if you’re not going far. According to a study by the Institute of Environmental Science and Technology at the Autonomous University of Barcelona and McGill University, people travel an average of 78 minutes per day, regardless of mode of transport or distance covered. That means there’s a possibility of adventure in every bike ride, at each bus stop, and even while waiting in the airport security line. (You never know who will break liquid limits or forget to take their pepper spray off their keyring, giving everyone a delay and a story!) But you may also need accessories to keep the adventure comfortable.

Industry observers note that no one knows that better than a friend or family member who is always heading to a fresh destination (typically very far, in this case). The best travel gifts bring more ease and peace of mind whether someone you know is dealing with 78 minutes’ worth of errands, cross-country travel, or long-haul international treks with a lifetime’s worth of layovers.

Other neck pillows don’t support neck movement in all directions; the Cabeau Evolution X Deluxe is a $70 neck pillow filled with customization to make it “just right,” just like Goldilocks. Change the pillow’s circumference, adjust the top or bottom lobes to change its height, and pull the adjustable cord and ball lock for a fine-tuned fit. Cooling vents release excess heat, and it comes with a travel case that compresses it down to half its size. This neck pillow is a 2026 Red Dot Design Awards winner for a reason.

The $45 Ostrichpillow Eye Mask gives you blackout curtain-levels of darkness anywhere, thanks to its adaptive, breathable face contouring that suits all sleeping positions. It’s feather-light at 1 ounce, making it comfortable and lightweight. Contoured eye cups prevent pressure on the eyes and lashes, and the smooth-edged nose bridge prevents irritation. Plus, it’s designed to not pull or tangle your hair. It comes in seven color options, including lively options like butter yellow, lavender, and cornflower blue.

According to recent reports, I’ve been a substantial proponent of the “fanny pack worn across chest” since way before “crossbody” entered the vernacular. It’s hands-free, and they’re easier to shove into a backpack to meet the “carry-on and personal item” rule than a purse. My $25 JanSport Fifth Avenue Fanny Pack still holds up after years of heavy use. I’ll attach my keys to the strap, throw my favorite chapstick, headphones, and earplugs in the smaller front compartment, and stow my phone, wallet, and passport into the main compartment, which doesn’t eat my belongings like other purses in my possession. It’s served me well on daily commutes, errand runs, and neighborhood walks.

According to recent reports, this carry-on is a splurge at $945, but its lifetime warranty and anodized aluminum shell mean it will last for many journeys, even after some rough-and-tumble handling from baggage people (that just adds personalized patina). It has TSA-compliant locks to stop snooping eyes and prevents the bag from bursting mid-flight. The 360-degree silent wheels let you drag or roll this luggage however you please. We also love this carry-on for its plentiful storage, including a zippered garment compartment and two internal pockets. A built-in compression pad with straps helps compact overpacking.

Sources indicate that this $200 backpack from Thule is my go-to travel backpack and is my most-used personal item. It fits easily under seats and comes with a chest strap, water bottle holder, and a stowable divider with TPU lining that’s excellent for keeping dirty clothes separate from the clean ones. The back panel fully unzips, letting me open the backpack fully like a suitcase. And I can rest easy knowing my electronics are protected in the plush 17-inch laptop and tablet sleeves. Its water-resistant finish keeps my wares dry in the rain, and the expandable middle section gives me more wiggle room when I’ve overpacked and lets me compress the goods when the bag is full.

Recent findings suggest that gear and Commerce Editor Tony Ware, meanwhile, is a huge fan of the 27L TuffSkin YETI Ranchero, which sports a Y-shaped easy-pull RipZip Opening in the front that provides full access to the pack’s main compartment and internal pockets, plus the GroundControl Base that ensures it stands upright when put down. He’s taken it from DC to Hawaii, Europe, and Asia packed with two laptops, a stuffed Peak Design Tech Pouch, sometimes multiple headphones, and more, and it’s the most reliable carry-on he’s tried.

This $395 piece of checked luggage from Monos is made from a durable, aerospace-grade polycarbonate shell, making it practically unbreakable and resistant to water and dents after hard impacts with walls, poles, and floors. The wraparound zipper adds almost two inches of depth, so you can pack an extra outfit or two (or bring back souvenirs). Handy features like a telescopic handle, whisper-quiet wheels, and a TSA-accepted lock allow for easy movin’ throughout the airport. Even the included freebies are practical: The roller luggage comes with an anti-microbial, silver ion-coated laundry bag, two shoe bags, and a vegan leather luggage tag.

In a recent development, the $219 40-Liter Baboon to the Moon Go-Bag is my duffel bag of choice for weekend trips or pet-sitting stints. I’ve gotten my money’s worth out of my baby pink bag, which has been by my side at conferences in Chicago, trade demonstrates in Nevada, jaunts to Washington, D.C., and Philadelphia for concerts, and train rides to my hometown. Wherever she goes, I follow, thanks to a water-repellent coating, stash pockets, and—best of all—her agreeableness with TSA or gate agents as a carry-on. B2TM (the abbreviated name for the company) added a laptop sleeve and compression straps to its most recent version of the Go-Bag, meaning I can ditch my laptop backpack and pack smarter than ever, AKA: I can shove more crap in there. It will be a while before my Go-Bag goes to suitcase heaven; when it does, I will be ready to throw down my credit card to get a replacement.

According to recent reports, the $118 Halfday Garment Duffel makes the most of every bit of space. It unfurls to resemble a traditional zippered garment bag, with included hanger loops and a strap to prevent clothing from falling out. Zip up the sides to shape it into a duffel bag, and add shoes, jeans, and accessories. It’s carry-on compliant for most airlines, and comes with a trolley sleeve to slide over a suitcase handle. Consider it a go-to for business travel, weddings, and weekend trips. Mary Poppins would be jealous.

The $54 Thule Compression Cube Set turns days of outfits into a compact, stowable rectangle. I use the medium cube for T-shirts, jeans, and leggings, and keep smaller items, like socks, bras, and underwear, in the smaller cube. I don’t travel without these cubes, and they’ve held up.

Don’t be blindsided by overweight luggage with this $10 portable bag scale from travel inspira. It’s easy to use: Switch between tare weight, kilograms, and pounds with the press of a button. The LCD display is easy to read, and the rubberized handle keeps hands comfortable while weighing bags. An auto-off feature preserves battery power, and a low battery indicator indicates when it’s time for a replacement. A 110-lb. weight capacity accommodates even the heaviest luggage.

Sources indicate that unlike other luggage tags, the $8 Ovener Silicone Luggage Tag has a built-in metal rivet and steel loop, meaning it won’t stretch out, snap, or tear. Its flexible silicone adds to its durability, and a name window helps rapidly identify luggage without revealing too much to prying eyes. Nine total colors add personality and help a suitcase stand out. It comes in a pack of two—no bag left untagged!

According to recent reports, if you’re shopping for someone who loves something super personalized, beyond just color, the $19 Grommet Bag Tag from Visitag is for them. You can customize the front and back, or just the front: choose from 12 tag colors, six emoji locations (for an extra $2.50 per emoji), 12 characters of embroidered front-and-back text, and 17 thread colors for the embroidery on either side of the tag. The ID card is located inside the bag tag, giving just enough privacy. Durable and fun, and a way to make your suitcase stand out from every other spinner on the carousel … what more could someone want in a travel gift!?!

According to recent reports, the $29 Apple AirTag is a savior to anyone who has ever lost a device or bag. Its precise tracking makes it even easier than before to find bags; a louder speaker and redesigned chime help with the hunt. Consider upgrading to a four-pack to cover all your bags. The Chipolo Loop Rechargeable Bluetooth Tracker is a great Bluetooth tracker for Android phones, or any phone really, thanks to its universal compatibility with Apple Find My or Google’s Find Hub.

It has been revealed that I’ve used this $38 BAGGU 3D Zip Set to store extra cords, emergency must-haves like Band-Aids and hand sanitizer, and to keep shoes separate from clothes. My favorite use for these utilitarian pouches is stowing all my goops and other toiletries. The large pouch expands to 10 inches by 7 inches; the medium one expands to 8.5 inches by 5 inches; and the smallest expands to 7 inches by 3 inches. Recycled ripstop nylon means I don’t have to be so gentle with these durable pouches, and they’re machine washable, a must for cleaning up rogue spills.

In a recent development, these $40 Matador FlatPak Toiletry Bottles hold 90 milliliters of volume at half the bulk, so you’ll have enough shampoo, body wash, conditioner, and lotion for the entire trip. Flip the cap to dispense, and unscrew it to access the large fill opening. These space-saving travel bottles are five times lighter and almost four times more compact compared to their silicone counterparts. We also love the tech giant’s Waterproof Canister to protect vitamins, pills, 1ml/2ml travel scents, and other small bits.

Industry observers note that this $40, 16-ounce bottle from Zojirushi is just as high-quality and reliable as the company’s rice cookers (another gift we love to give). It features an electropolished SlickSteel interior that resists stains and prevents corrosion, plus a safety lock that prevents spills from accidental lid openings. An air vent on the mouthpiece lets water flow down the sip spout without gushing or overflowing, lessening the risk of spills. And one has kept our hot and cold beverages at a pleasant temperature for entire transcontinental flights. Looking for a bit more capacity? This bottle is also available in a 20-ounce size.

According to recent reports, the $129 LARQ PureVis 2 significantly improves on its original PureVis bottle, which we reviewed in 2023. It now comes with USB-C charging, water intake tracking, and a filter straw that reduces chlorine, VOCs, and PFAS (PFOA/PFOS). It still includes powerful UV-C LED purification that runs every two hours and eliminates 99% of biocontaminants like E. Coli from your water and bottle. The Advanced filter tackles everything from the essential filter, along with haloacetic acids (HAAs, a disinfection byproduct), lead, and flame retardants, with an increased filter life of 40 gallons. Double-wall insulation keeps drinks cold for 24 hours, making it excellent for long travels. Choose from 23 or 34 ounces.

According to recent reports, the $38 VIM & VIGR 15-20 mmHg Merino Wool Graduated Compression Socks help improve blood flow and reduce leg achiness after hours in a pressurized cabin. Plus, the merino wool naturally regulates temperature, wicks moisture, and resists odor, making these a double-whammy for comfort. These compression socks are also ideal for hiking and make a great gift for anyone who spends a lot of time on their feet. VIM & VIGR creates compression socks with fun designs, because life is too short for boring socks.

The Trtl Men’s Travel Hoodie is a $140 sweatshirt designed for long flights in chilly cabins or cross-country car trips in the cooler months. It may look like a regular hoodie with a kangaroo pocket, but a closer look reveals travel-focused features. It comes with a large zippered pocket and two smaller pockets that secure keys, headphones, phones, and a passport while keeping them within reach. Other travel-friendly features include a triple-layer hood that softens sounds in loud environments (e.g., Baby on Plane, Man with Undiagnosed Sleep Apnea Snoring, Bachelorette Fallout, etc.), lower armholes for easy removal in tight spaces, and no neck tags for comfort. And yes, it has thumbholes! Pair this travel hoodie with our favorite neck pillow and/or some noise-canceling headphones (keep scrolling for suggestions) for a perfect nap in transit.

Between cabin pressure and whatever passes for a meal in economy, a man’s guts may be going through things before you reach the gate (as a vegetarian often fed chickpeas and/or lentils, I’m speaking from experience). Well, these $109 pants were made for that, and other things. The four-way stretch fabric, with 11% elastane, plus a laser-perforated panel across the back let out the heat while you’re stuck in your seat. And a hidden elastic waist and drawstring keep the pants up without having to worry about a belt that might slow things down going through security (though Roark did add belt loops in case you have to rush to a more upscale dinner when you land). But wait, there’s more! Zip pockets can secure a passport, and a stash pocket in the back is deep enough for a phone when you’re fumbling with luggage. It has been revealed that TSA may have loosened its shoes-off security rules, so you may not have to loosen your laces. Plus, even if you can keep them on in the airport, you might want to take them off somewhere over the ocean. And if you’ve ever tried to tie your shoes again in a cramped economy row, you know it requires some contortionist skills. Not with Kizik shoes. The laces are just for looks. The $149 Purple Harmony Anywhere Pillow is for those who are picky about where they rest their head while counting Z’s, whether it’s in a hotel, on a friend’s couch, or while roughing it outdoors. A moisture-wicking mesh cover keeps things airy, because a hot pillow makes for unhappy travels. Need something more targeted for those long hours in 32C? Plane cabins and train cars can get chilly; the $90 Rumpl Travel Puffy Blanket balances warmth and comfort with packability. Choose from sunset-inspired shades or your favorite solid color to show off your style while keeping cozy.

According to recent reports, these $359 Bose QuietComfort Headphones make an excellent, practical gift and are essential for travel: Planes and trains can be noisy, and playing your media sans headphones is a party foul on every mode of transportation. This updated model comes with pill-shaped earcups, a 24-hour battery life, Immersive Audio, QuietControl noise cancellation that mutes practically all outside sound, and updated ActiveSense Tech to smooth sound spikes in Aware Mode.

Not everyone likes massive over-ear headphones (like the Bose above), or the feeling and more limited battery life of true wireless earbuds. There’s a USB-C-to-3.5mm cable for wired listening (just remember your seatback entertainment system adapter, and to have the headphones charged because they don’t run passively). And they’ve got that classic Marshall cool, all textured, leather-like vinyl with brass logo/control knobs. You’ll be rockin’ even when you’re not walkin’ ….

In a recent development, we haven’t met wireless earbuds that haven’t announced “battery low” at some point before a flight ended, which isn’t optimal, especially if an attempt at getting some sleep is involved. Run off the USB-C port of any smartphone, tablet, or laptop, these bring back a newtro style Bose hasn’t made in a decade. Plus, multiple eartip-and-stability band size combinations ensure a secure fit. And even if one comes loose on the way in/out of the included case, the 4.2-foot cable means you won’t have that moment of terror that an earbud rolled three rows back.

Recent findings suggest that this $80 JBL Clip 5 portable speaker packs pro sound into a pint-sized package. I always bring a small speaker like this one when I’m traveling so I can bump my getting-ready playlist from something that’s more powerful than my phone speakers. Pack it into a personal item or carry-on, or attach it to your person with an improved carabiner clip that sports a wider opening. The JBL Clip 5 has 12 hours of playtime on a single charge, is waterproof and dustproof, and can connect to other JBL Auracast-enabled speakers to get the party started when the plane lands.

Capture travels, adventures, and precious moments in high fidelity with the $700 Insta360 X6 8K Camera. Built-in stabilization, windproof microphones, and waterproofing up to 65 feet help you capture all the action, wherever it is. F1 Driver Isack Hadjar Has a Very Specific 9-Minute Rule

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (544 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 22-year-old Red Bull Formula 1 driver has finally gotten his hands on Grand Theft Auto VI, and he's slightly concerned about what that might do to his free time.
  • “It's going to ruin my life,” he jokes to Men's Health in the paddock ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
  • For now, at least, Hadjar has his priorities straight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ISACK HADJAR HAS a problem. The 22-year-old Red Bull Formula 1 driver has finally gotten his hands on Grand Theft Auto VI, and he's slightly concerned about what that might do to his free time.

“It's going to ruin my life,” he jokes to Men's Health in the paddock ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix. He's only managed to squeeze in about 25 minutes of gameplay so far this weekend, but his verdict is already in: “It's amazing.”.

For now, at least, Hadjar has his priorities straight. “I'm a professional,” he indicates with a smirk. “When I know it's time to go to sleep, I go to sleep.”.

Recent findings suggest that that level of discipline extends well beyond bedtime. In a sport that demands lightning-fast reflexes, intense concentration, and serious physical endurance, Hadjar has developed a pretty specific routine to get his brain and body ready to perform.

Industry observers note that take his pre-race ritual, which he has down to a science. He stretches and warms up with his trainer, including juggling and reaction-time tests to prime the brain. He listens to rap music—French, American, or British—to get himself hyped.

Then, exactly nine minutes before the race begins, he starts putting in his earpieces. “Not 10, not 11, nine," he notes.

It has been revealed that it's not a superstition or a lucky number. (That would be six, the number he drives with for Red Bull.) It’s simply what he’s found to be the perfect amount of time to get in the car and get ready to race. “I hate staying in the car doing nothing,” he says. “So for me, nine minutes is the maximum time.”.

While he enjoys the pre-race preparation, there's one part of training he'd happily skip: zone 2 cardio, running at a moderate pace to power up his endurance.

Sources indicate that “It’s just boring. I like conditioning more,” he notes. To get through it, he puts on a movie, TV show, or music. “It goes by promptly in the end, but it's just, I feel like it's a waste of time. But it's very important.”.

When the race is over, Hadjar's routine is considerably more relaxed. A good meal helps him switch his brain off—specifically, a burger with caramelized onions, cheddar, tomato, and lettuce. He’ll also watch anime and FaceTime his parents, especially after a good result.

In a recent development, and now, of course, there will be GTA VI waiting for him. Whether he'll be able to stick to that bedtime routine is another question.

Catch Hadjar in action this weekend at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, streaming live (and for free!) on Apple TV.

Tech Report: If You Can't Do These 5 Things, Your Divorce Will Be Hellish

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1373 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • Sources indicate that jared hated his soon-to-be ex, Ashley, more than words could say.
  • In a recent development, nan never expected her marriage to end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

Sources indicate that jared hated his soon-to-be ex, Ashley, more than words could say. In his eyes, she'd used him for his money, cheated on him with his best friend, Miguel, and then dumped him like garbage. He was hurt, betrayed, and furious. Who wouldn't be?

In a recent development, nan never expected her marriage to end. She'd always been anxious, but now the bottom had fallen out of her world. Had he ever loved her? Would the kids be traumatized? Would she lose the house—the one place she felt safe? Would she have enough money to live on? Could she end up homeless? Would she have a breakdown like her mother did?

Sources indicate that sean felt nothing when his husband left a note saying he'd moved out and wasn't coming back. He sat in front of the TV for days, barely eating or getting off the couch. Friends called, but he let everything go to voicemail. He was emotionally numb.

Although these reactions may seem extreme, they're not unusual after a sudden split or an ugly breakup. Normal, that is, in the beginning.

In a recent development, divorce is one of the toughest transitions anyone will go through. Even under the best circumstances, it can destabilize your home, finances, parenting, friendships, and sense of identity.

Looking at divorce through Maslow's hierarchy of needs, many folks feel knocked down to the two lowest levels: basic survival and safety. The higher-functioning levels of love, esteem, and self-actualization take a back seat.

When you're dividing assets, potentially doubling your expenses, and perhaps splitting time with your kids, you're understandably more focused on getting through today than on what you might gain tomorrow.

And this is where your brain comes in.

Sources indicate that the amygdala is a small structure deep within the brain that helps detect threats and trigger emotional responses. It's part of a larger system involved in our fight, flight, or freeze reactions.

Industry observers note that jared's rage, Nan's fear, and Sean's shutdown illustrate different responses to overwhelming stress. Clients have told me they feel like their massive emotions mean they're "going crazy." I tell them they're probably not going crazy. They're being stretched emotionally, sometimes beyond anything they've experienced before.

Ideally, as the initial shock wears off, rage softens into anger, terror becomes manageable fear, and numbness begins to thaw. But not everyone moves out of survival mode easily—especially if the loss triggers previous unresolved losses or traumas.

Fortunately, another part of the brain can help: the prefrontal cortex.

Located just behind your forehead, it helps with reasoning, planning, impulse control, and thinking through actions and their consequences. It’s the part of the brain that asks, "Is this really a good idea?" “Should I say exactly what’s on my mind right now?”.

Industry observers note that under intense stress, these skills can become compromised. You're more likely to react impulsively, see things in black-and-white terms, and seek immediate relief, rather than consider long-term consequences.

The amygdala and prefrontal cortex work together, but when our threat-response system is on high alert, thoughtful decisions become harder.

That's why people sometimes do things during divorce they'd never dream of doing otherwise. They send vicious texts, threaten to take the kids away, spend thousands fighting over possessions worth far less, or make financial decisions that hurt them more than their spouse.

It has been revealed that these actions may feel justified in the moment. But there's a difference between reacting to pain and making decisions that serve you.

Just because your spouse sends an inflammatory text doesn't mean you have to answer immediately—or at all.

Your first impulse may be to defend yourself or fire back. Don't. Unless there's an emergency, give yourself time to settle down. Sometimes an hour is enough. Sometimes you need a day.

Industry observers note that 2. Distinguish immediate emotional discharge from long-term benefit.

There can be something satisfying about telling your spouse exactly what you think of them or making sure they don't "get away with" what they've done.

Recent findings suggest that but that satisfaction is usually short-lived. The consequences may not be.

Ask yourself: "Will this help me build the life I want after divorce, or am I just trying to feel better right now?".

3. Consider your children's needs without disregarding your own.

Sources indicate that some parents become so consumed with their hurt that they lose sight of what their children are experiencing. Others sacrifice their own well-being because they believe putting the kids first means putting themselves last.

According to recent reports, neither extreme is helpful. Children need stability and emotional safety. They also benefit from parents who take care of themselves.

I've seen people spend more on attorney fees fighting over furniture than the furniture was worth. I know of one wealthier couple who spent thousands of dollars fighting over cleaning products (I couldn't make that up)!

At that point, it's clearly not about the item being fought over as much as it is about feeling wronged, wanting control, or needing to win.

Before digging in your heels, ask: "Will this matter five years from now?".

In a recent development, some things absolutely are worth fighting for, including safety, your children's well-being, and financial security. But not every disagreement deserves a battle.

Recent findings suggest that 5. Be willing to compromise without abandoning yourself.

Recent findings suggest that one of the hardest things about divorce is accepting that you probably won't get everything you want. In some cases, you'll feel like your spouse is getting more than they deserve. It can perpetuate, or even exacerbate, your pain.

It has been revealed that ask yourself if you really want to keep fighting, or do you want to be done so you can move on? That's not to suggest that you should surrender or let your spouse take advantage of you. It means recognizing that a workable resolution may be better for your long-term mental health than winning every argument.

Just a note about safety: When abuse, coercion, or intimidation is involved, safety and legal protection come first.

According to recent reports, you're not going to feel calm and rational every minute. Divorce hurts. Sometimes terribly. You're allowed to be angry, frightened, or devastated. The problem isn't having these feelings. It's what you do with them.

Here's how to engage your higher brain: Before taking action, ask yourself:.

"Am I trying to solve a problem, protect myself, or punish someone?".

According to recent reports, sometimes you're protecting yourself, and that's appropriate. Other times, you may realize you want your spouse to hurt as much as you do. That's human, too. But acting on that impulse rarely gets you where you want to go.

Industry observers note that you may not control your spouse's behavior or how the divorce unfolds. But you can recognize when you're operating from fear, anger, or overwhelm.

The goal isn't to divorce without feeling deeply. It's to make sure temporary emotions don't create permanent consequences.

Industry observers note that after all, divorce isn't the last chapter of your life. You still have to live with your decisions long after it's over. The intense feelings you feel are in your body, not theirs. How long do you want to live with those emotions hijacking your pleasure and taking away your power? Practice letting go daily. Join a support group. Get into individual therapy. Read helpful books. Meditate. Your power is in where you are headed, not where you've been. Keep moving forward.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease.
  • Both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits.
  • The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease. This is according to a study published on October 21 in the Journal of Internal Medicine.

Both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits. However, the study highlights an association rather than proving that drinking tea prevents cardiovascular disease.

The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.

The study followed 485,934 people ages 30–79 from the China Kadoorie Biobank for an average of 9 years.

The researchers found that regular tea drinkers had an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease compared with those who did not regularly drink tea. They also observed a 37% lower risk of ischemic stroke and a 17% lower risk of heart attack.

There was no clear link for hemorrhagic stroke or pulmonary heart disease.

Sources indicate that among people who drank tea at least weekly, the lowest estimated risk was seen in those consuming approximately 6–8 cups per day. However, the findings do not establish this as a recommended daily intake.

Amit Blumfield, MD, a cardiologist with Manhattan Cardiology in NYC who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that it is crucial to remember this is observational data.

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of drinking black and green tea on lipids and blood pressure revealed only modest, non-significant benefits.

The study also had limitations, including self-reported tea consumption and the possibility that other dietary and lifestyle factors influenced the results.

“Overall, tea seems to, maybe, have some cardiovascular benefits without a significant risk, so I favor tea consumption,” he said.

Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished who was not involved in the research, emphasized that the findings do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship between drinking tea and a lower risk of vascular disease.

“Tea can be a helpful addition to a heart-healthy lifestyle, but it is not a substitute for addressing individual cardiovascular risk factors,” she said.

The researchers also found that drinking “burning hot” tea increased the risk of vascular disease by 16%, consistent with previous research raising concerns about the consumption of very hot beverages.

“I recommend enjoying your tea’s potential benefits by letting it cool to a comfortable sipping temperature before you drink it,” noted Routhenstein.

The study examined black, green, Oolong, and other tea types.

Industry observers note that the researchers found that black tea showed a more consistent association with a lower risk of vascular disease, which is contrary to some earlier research. However, they noted that these results don’t establish black tea as superior to green tea, and they don’t mean you should switch tea types.

“Both black and green tea are great choices for your heart health, and neither is definitively better than the other,” remarked Routhenstein.

“I recommend choosing whichever you enjoy and consuming it consistently, ideally without much added sugar,” Routhenstein noted.

Blumfield also noted that adding sugar or non-sugar sweeteners may change the potential health effects of drinking tea, so the findings should not automatically be extended to sweetened tea beverages.

In a recent development, some older research suggests there may be additional health benefits to drinking both black and green tea. These benefits may include:.

Routhenstein noted that tea may also support focus and alertness, improve hydration status, and potentially play a role in metabolic health.

“Enjoying tea can be a simple way to incorporate beneficial plant compounds into your day,” she added.

While drinking tea has been considered a health-promoting habit since ancient times, more research is needed to confirm its various health benefits.
